data.long_meaning: Derived from the Old English elements 'ing' (maiden) and 'gunna' (strong yew), Ingunna represents the strength and resilience of a young woman. This name was popular in Anglo-Saxon England and carries a rich history and cultural significance. The name Ingunna carries the meaning “Maiden of the strong yew” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Ingunna usually hope their child will grow to embody maiden of the strong yew and live with faith, good character and purpose.
